INTERFACE/GLUES/MODELS/UI_GOBLIN/UI_GOBL.note: F-151 goblin character-select scene — the retroport ships fov 0.97 rad where the Cata 4.3.4 original authors 0.84571, so the frustum falls outside the built set and the bottom-right corner renders empty. Blizzard's authored value still tested short (our char-select leaves bare the corner Cata's creation panels covered), so we go to 0.75 — the same value ui_worgen.m2 carries.

INTERFACE/GLUES/MODELS/UI_ALLIANCE/UI_AL.note: F-151 human character-select/create scene. THIS is the human scene, NOT UI_HUMAN: GlueParent.lua SetBackgroundModel() special-cases the race name and redirects HUMAN -> UI_ALLIANCE\UI_Alliance.m2 (and ORC -> UI_HORDE), so UI_HUMAN.M2 is shipped but never loaded by any code path. Editing UI_HUMAN is inert - that mistake cost a client round trip (2026-09-30). Camera sits at (-4.365, 3.849, 0.575) aiming at (2.291, -1.063, 1.073), 8.287 away; the position and target tracks are 2-key all-zero, so these base vectors are the live values. fov: shipped 0.87 framed 5.13 world units wide at the subject; 0.70 was still too far out in play, 0.60 frames 3.84 and is right. pan: at 0.60 the frame is 2.88 tall at 16:9 and the subject's feet sat on the bottom edge, so the aim drops 0.2884 = 10% of frame height (a 1.99 deg downward tilt), which moves the scene up in frame and opens margin under the feet. The camera itself does not move, so distance and perspective are unchanged. To retune: dz = -(share) * 2 * 8.287 * tan(fov/2) / (16/9).

INTERFACE/GLUES/MODELS/UI_ALLIANCE_CREAT.note: F-151 character CREATE scene. Both screens run through GlueParent.lua SetBackgroundModel(), and character create calls it for the whole Alliance faction (CharacterCreate.lua: faction == "Alliance" -> SetBackgroundModel(CharacterCreate, "HUMAN")), so the character-select camera edit landed on the creation screen too. GlueParent now points character create at this copy and character select at UI_ALLIANCE. Published via copy_from so it is derived at build time from the upstream pack, not an untracked duplicate binary in source-assets; the skins come along beside it because the client derives <model path minus extension>NN.skin - keep their filenames, change only the folder. Camera: restoring the donor's 0.87 was still too zoomed in for this screen, so it widens to 1.00 (frame 9.05 across the subject vs 7.70 at 0.87, +18%). 1.00 is the practical ceiling: rasterising the 19408 triangles of UI_Alliance00.skin through camera[0] shows the scene fills the frame completely through 0.95, and at 1.00 the only gap is a sliver in the BOTTOM-LEFT corner (0.8% of the border ring) which this screen's race/class panel covers. 1.05 opens it to 2.4% and 1.20 tears the frame apart. Do not widen past 1.00 without re-running the coverage sweep.
